Plot predictions across epidemiological scenarios

Source: R/plot_scenarios.R
plot_scenarios.Rd

Plot predictions generated by `simulate_scenarios()` while respecting both the scenario design created by `simulate_ranges()` (`"grid"` or `"paired"`) and the prediction output returned by `simulate_scenarios()` (`"samples"` or `"summary"`).

Usage

plot_scenarios(
  data,
  x,
  scenario_type = c("grid", "paired"),
  output = c("auto", "samples", "summary"),
  mode = NULL,
  y = "prediction",
  facet = NULL,
  sample = "sample",
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  scale_factor = 1,
  facet_ncol = NULL,
  facet_nrow = NULL,
  color_scale = NULL,
  color_label = "Sample",
  line_color = "black",
  ribbon_fill = "black",
  ribbon_alpha = 1,
  show_ribbon = TRUE,
  smooth = TRUE,
  smooth_method = NULL,
  smooth_formula = NULL,
  smooth_se = FALSE,
  line_width = NULL,
  line_alpha = 1,
  paired_samples_geom = c("boxplot", "jitter"),
  boxplot_color = "black",
  boxplot_fill = "white",
  boxplot_width = NULL,
  jitter_color = "black",
  jitter_width = 0.12,
  jitter_alpha = 0.65,
  jitter_size = NULL,
  pointrange_color = "black",
  point_size = NULL,
  pointrange_linewidth = NULL,
  paired_x_discrete = TRUE,
  x_breaks = ggplot2::waiver(),
  y_breaks = ggplot2::waiver(),
  x_limits = NULL,
  y_limits = NULL,
  x_expand = NULL,
  y_expand = ggplot2::waiver(),
  x_label = "Exposure",
  y_label = "Predicted",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  base_size = 10,
  text_face = "bold",
  axis_title_size = 12,
  strip_background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"),
  legend_position = "none",
  line_args = list(),
  ribbon_args = list(),
  boxplot_args = list(),
  jitter_args = list(),
  pointrange_args = list(),
  point_args = list(),
  add = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A non-empty data frame returned by `simulate_scenarios()`.

x

Character scalar naming the scenario variable shown on the x-axis.

scenario_type

Character. Scenario design used to generate the scenarios in `simulate_ranges()`. Must be `"grid"` or `"paired"`. Default is `"grid"`.

output

Character. Prediction output represented by `data`: `"auto"`, `"samples"`, or `"summary"`.

With `"auto"` (default), the function identifies `"samples"` when the column named by `sample` is present; otherwise it uses `"summary"`. This mirrors the two output structures returned by `simulate_scenarios()`.

mode

Deprecated compatibility alias for `output`. It is retained so calls written for earlier versions of `plot_scenarios()` do not break. New code should use `output`. Do not supply both `output` and `mode`.

y

Character scalar naming the prediction column. Default is `"prediction"`.

facet

Optional character vector naming variables used by `ggplot2::facet_wrap()`, for example `c("wetness", "tmean")`.

sample

Character scalar naming the sample identifier in `output = "samples"`. Default is `"sample"`.

lower, upper

Optional character scalars naming the lower and upper uncertainty-limit columns in `output = "summary"`.

When left as `NULL`, `plot_scenarios()` looks first for `"prediction_lower"` and `"prediction_upper"`, respectively, and then for `"lower"` and `"upper"`.

These arguments are not used for `output = "samples"` because sample-level output contains individual prediction draws rather than pre-computed lower/upper limits.

scale_factor

Finite numeric multiplier applied to predictions and, when present, lower and upper limits. Use `100` to display proportions as percentages.

facet_ncol, facet_nrow

Optional positive integers controlling the facet arrangement.

color_scale

Optional ggplot2 color scale used for sample-specific grid trajectories. When `NULL`, `ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_c()` is used.

color_label

Legend title used by the default grid color scale.

line_color

Color of the central trajectory for grid-summary plots.

ribbon_fill, ribbon_alpha

Legacy argument names retained for backward compatibility. In grid-summary plots, `ribbon_fill` now controls the color of the dashed lower/upper interval curves and `ribbon_alpha` controls their transparency. Defaults reproduce the black dashed interval curves used by `plot_losses()`.

show_ribbon

Logical. Legacy argument name retained for backward compatibility. If `TRUE`, a grid-summary plot shows dashed lower/upper uncertainty curves when interval columns are available.

smooth

Logical. For grid plots, use `ggplot2::geom_smooth()` when `TRUE` (default) or `ggplot2::geom_line()` when `FALSE`.

smooth_method

Optional smoothing method passed to `ggplot2::geom_smooth()`. When `NULL`, ggplot2 chooses its default method.

smooth_formula

Optional formula passed to `ggplot2::geom_smooth()`.

smooth_se

Logical. Display the smoothing standard-error band produced by `geom_smooth()`. Default is `FALSE`. This is distinct from the prediction uncertainty represented by `lower` and `upper`.

line_width

Optional positive line width for grid trajectories. When `NULL`, ggplot2 uses its default.

line_alpha

Transparency of grid trajectories, between 0 and 1.

paired_samples_geom

Character. Geometry used when `scenario_type = "paired"` and `output = "samples"`. `"boxplot"` (default) displays the distribution of the sample predictions for each paired scenario; `"jitter"` displays the individual sample predictions.

boxplot_color, boxplot_fill

Color and fill used by the default paired sample boxplot.

boxplot_width

Optional positive box width for paired sample boxplots. When `NULL`, ggplot2 uses its default.

jitter_color

Color used for paired sample jittered points.

jitter_width

Horizontal jitter width for paired sample points.

jitter_alpha

Transparency of paired sample jittered points.

jitter_size

Optional positive size of paired sample jittered points. When `NULL`, ggplot2 uses its default.

pointrange_color

Color used by `ggplot2::geom_pointrange()` for paired summary plots.

point_size

Optional positive point size for paired-summary plots. When `NULL`, ggplot2 uses its default.

pointrange_linewidth

Optional positive line width for the uncertainty interval in paired-summary plots. When `NULL`, ggplot2 uses its default.

paired_x_discrete

Logical. For paired scenarios, treat the x variable as discrete when `TRUE` (default), matching a manual mapping such as `aes(as.factor(rain), ...)`. If `FALSE`, `x` must be numeric and a continuous x-axis is used.

x_breaks, y_breaks

Axis breaks. Defaults to `ggplot2::waiver()`, which lets ggplot2 choose breaks automatically and preserves axis tick labels and the `theme_bw()` panel grid. Use `NULL` only to intentionally remove the corresponding breaks and grid lines.

x_limits, y_limits

Optional axis limits.

For grid plots and paired plots with `paired_x_discrete = FALSE`, `x_limits` must be a finite numeric vector of length two.

For paired plots with `paired_x_discrete = TRUE`, `x_limits` can instead be a vector of observed x levels used to subset and/or order the displayed categories.

x_expand, y_expand

Axis expansion specifications.

When `x_expand = NULL`, continuous x-axes use `ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))`, matching the original EpiExposure scenario figure, while discrete paired x-axes retain ggplot2's default discrete expansion.

x_label, y_label

Axis titles. Defaults are `"Exposure"` and `"Predicted"`.

title, subtitle, caption

Optional plot annotations.

theme

Optional ggplot2 theme added after the default `theme_bw()` and EpiExposure text settings, allowing users to override them.

base_size

Base text size. Default is 10.

text_face

Common text face. Default is `"bold"`.

axis_title_size

Axis-title size. Default is 12.

strip_background

Facet-strip background element.

legend_position

Legend position. Default is `"none"`.

line_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to the active grid trajectory layer (`geom_smooth()` or `geom_line()`).

ribbon_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to both lower and upper uncertainty-curve layers in grid-summary mode. The legacy argument name is retained for backward compatibility.

boxplot_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_boxplot()` in paired-samples mode.

jitter_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_jitter()` when `paired_samples_geom = "jitter"`.

pointrange_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_pointrange()` in paired-summary mode.

point_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_point()` when summary predictions do not contain lower/upper uncertainty limits.

add

Optional ggplot2 component or list of components added last.

...

Additional named arguments passed to the principal geometry used for the selected combination of `scenario_type` and `output`.

Value

A `ggplot` object.

Details

The default plotting behavior is:

* `scenario_type = "grid"` + `output = "samples"`: sample-specific trajectories using `geom_smooth()` (or `geom_line()`). * `scenario_type = "grid"` + `output = "summary"`: one central trajectory, optionally with dashed lower/upper uncertainty curves. * `scenario_type = "paired"` + `output = "samples"`: the distribution of sample predictions at each paired scenario using `geom_boxplot()` by default. * `scenario_type = "paired"` + `output = "summary"`: point estimates and lower/upper uncertainty intervals using `geom_pointrange()`.

`scenario_type` and `output` describe different aspects of the data and should not be conflated:

* `scenario_type` describes how exposure scenarios were constructed by `simulate_ranges()`. * `output` describes how predictions were returned by `simulate_scenarios()`.

Consequently, all four combinations are valid.

For sample-level output, `lower` and `upper` are intentionally ignored. The uncertainty is represented by the multiple sample predictions themselves.

For summary output, lower and upper limits are used when available:

* grid + summary: the limits define dashed lower/upper uncertainty curves; * paired + summary: the limits define the vertical point-range.

If summary output does not contain lower/upper limits, the function still plots the central prediction: a grid trajectory for grid scenarios or points for paired scenarios.

For paired sample output, `geom_boxplot()` is the default because several prediction samples correspond to the same paired scenario value. The user can instead request the individual sample predictions with `paired_samples_geom = "jitter"`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. GRID + SAMPLES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
pred_grid_samples <- simulate_scenarios(
  fit = fit,
  scenarios = range_grid,
  data = sim_data,
  uncertainty = TRUE,
  output = "samples",
  n_samples = 20,
  seed = 1234
)

plot_scenarios(
  data = pred_grid_samples,
  x = "rain",
  scenario_type = "grid",
  output = "samples",
  facet = c("wetness", "tmean"),
  scale_factor = 100,
  x_limits = c(0, 15)
)

# Because output = "auto" is the default, the same plot can be requested as:
plot_scenarios(
  data = pred_grid_samples,
  x = "rain",
  scenario_type = "grid",
  facet = c("wetness", "tmean"),
  scale_factor = 100,
  x_limits = c(0, 15)
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. GRID + SUMMARY
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_scenarios(
  data = pred_grid_summary,
  x = "rain",
  scenario_type = "grid",
  output = "summary",
  facet = c("wetness", "tmean"),
  scale_factor = 100
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. PAIRED + SAMPLES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_scenarios(
  data = pred_paired_samples,
  x = "rain",
  scenario_type = "paired",
  output = "samples",
  scale_factor = 100,
  x_label = "Daily precipitation (mm)",
  y_label = "Predicted (%)"
)

# Show the individual sample predictions instead of boxplots:
plot_scenarios(
  data = pred_paired_samples,
  x = "rain",
  scenario_type = "paired",
  output = "samples",
  paired_samples_geom = "jitter",
  scale_factor = 100
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. PAIRED + SUMMARY
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_scenarios(
  data = pred_paired_summary,
  x = "rain",
  scenario_type = "paired",
  output = "summary",
  scale_factor = 100,
  x_label = "Daily precipitation (mm)",
  y_label = "Predicted (%)"
)
} # }
